newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul blue chips seen falling on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul blue chips seen falling on consolidation.

text.p: South Korean blue chips are likely to fall on Wednesday as investors believed the stocks were overvalued in view of the lack of fresh optimistic signs about the economy, brokers said.
Small-capitalised individual stocks will instead draw attention, but the composite index would remain negative due to the blue-chip weakness, they said.
"Economic optimism sparked by the June trade surplus is seen fading as no more good news has come," said Kim Dae-hee, researcher at LG Securities.
The composite index fell 5.77 points to 767.74 on Tuesday.
Last week's announcement of the first monthly trade surplus in 30 months raised hopes that the economy had bottomed out.

Brokers said chipmakers would continue to face selling on worries about falling memory chip prices. The spot price of 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips are now below $7 per unit, against this year's peak of more than $10 in April.
But Hyundai Securities analyst Koh Kyung-bae said chipmakers would rebound after the past two days of declines.
